Container.Name: watchstate
Container.Overview: WatchState syncs watched / unwatched state between media servers (Plex, Jellyfin, Emby) and between the users of one server, with a web UI for backends, users, tasks and logs. EXTRA PARAMETERS (set these in the live container, not in this template): --user 99:100 . The publisher's manual Unraid install requires it; set it before the first start, and if files already exist under the Config path with another owner, run chown -R 99:100 on that folder. CONFIG: set the Config path to a folder on a pool. It holds the database, the backend tokens and the schedule, so treat it as a secret store and back it up. NETWORK: leave Network bridge. Backends are reached by URL from inside the container, so use the media server's own LAN address, not localhost. TIMEZONE: set TZ to the same zone as the media servers; the publisher's FAQ says they must agree or state changes are skipped as stale. SCHEDULE AND BACKENDS: both are configured in the web UI (Configuration > Env, Backends), not through this template. HEALTH: the image defines no health check and the publisher documents none; a working web UI at the host port is the check.
Container.Description: Syncs watched state between media servers and between users, with a web UI. Needs one host port and one config folder.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: Host port for the web UI; the container always listens on 8080 internally - change the host side only. The publisher's install instructions map 8080 to 8080.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Host folder for the database, backend tokens and schedule, e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/watchstate. Must be owned by 99:100 (see Extra Parameters in the Overview). The publisher's install instructions mount their data folder at /config.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone, same as your media servers (for example America/Chicago). The publisher's FAQ names TZ as the Docker fallback when WS_TZ is not set in the web UI.
